migrationRenumbering.reason: 20260923-26 are occupied on canonical by legacy-cutover (20260923/24), operational-alert (20260925/26) and neighbours. Reusing them would collide.

correction1_noApplicationReachableBypass.whatWasWrong: The append-only guard opened for any session that had set `closure_evidence.migration_operation` (UPDATE) or `closure_evidence.retention_operation` (DELETE). A GUC is a session variable, not a privilege — the application's own pool holds UPDATE/DELETE rights and could set either value for itself. The mechanism authorized nothing.
correction1_noApplicationReachableBypass.whyItWasThere: The snapshot backfill had to write to a table an earlier migration had already sealed. The door was a workaround for an ordering mistake.
howItIsFixedStructurally: 20261008 adds the exemption column, runs the one-time backfill while the ledger is still mutable, installs the BEFORE INSERT trigger forcing snapshot_exempt=false, adds the snapshot CHECK, and installs immutability LAST.
The guard now refuses UPDATE and DELETE unconditionally: no current_setting, no named operation, no branch reading anything the caller controls.
correction1_noApplicationReachableBypass.retentionPosition: Removing evidence is not an application operation. It requires ownership of the table — a privilege Postgres checks and the runtime role does not have. A genuine legal-retention or erasure obligation needs a privileged database role and an operator workflow, and is a separate decision that has not been taken.

literalTests.claim: An ordinary session that sets BOTH former door settings still cannot UPDATE or DELETE
literalTests.note: The test asserts the settings really landed (current_setting returns 'authorized' / 'snapshot_exemption_backfill') before asserting the refusal, so a refusal for the wrong reason cannot look like success.

literalTests.claim: The installed guard function contains no session-variable branch at all
literalTests.note: Reads pg_proc.prosrc — a behavioural test only probes the values someone thought to try.

literalTests.claim: A new computed-hash row without a snapshot is refused
A new row that asks for snapshot_exempt=true is still refused — the trigger overwrites the claim before the CHECK sees it
Deleting the parent closure request, and the initiative, are both refused by RESTRICT
Deleting the SOURCE leaves the evidence citing it intact
Late upgrade preserves the historical row, stamps it exempt, leaves its hash intact, adds the CHECK, and leaves no bypass behind

correction2_toolOutputThroughTheRealProd.whatWasWrong: Every tool_output test wrote the tool_outputs row itself. That proves the reader agrees with the fixture, not with the system — and it is how the source's misclassification survived so long.
correction2_toolOutputThroughTheRealProd.realChain: POST /api/tools/:id/promote (tools.routes.ts → ToolController.promoteToOutput → ensureToolOutputSnapshot → tool_outputs) → closure evidence attach (initiativeClosure.routes.ts → addEvidence → closureEvidenceSourceReader) → cold readback through a new Pool.
correction2_toolOutputThroughTheRealProd.fixtureIsASessionNotAnArtefact: The test seeds a dynamic-swot session whose moves genuinely clear the engine's W2 gate (rationale, live links, complete trade-off, named rejected alternative). A session that fails any of those yields zero conclusions and the freeze path refuses it outright, so a frozen row is itself proof the contract was met.

assertedOnProductionOutput.note: computeOutputHash is FNV-1a over 64 BITS, documented in sharedRuntime/toolOutputs/contentHash.ts as non-cryptographic. This is asserted on a value production code computed, not on a fixture constant.

negativeControls: Forged producer digest on an otherwise genuine payload → 409 content_hash_mismatch, 0 rows.
Client-supplied sourceHash / sourceVersionId / snapshotExempt in the request body → ignored; the stored identity is the computed one and snapshot_exempt is false.
A tool output frozen in another tenant → 404 EVIDENCE_REF_NOT_FOUND.
Source drift after the pin, with the payload AND digest rewritten so the row stays internally consistent → 409 EVIDENCE_SOURCE_VERSION_CONFLICT and the pinned evidence unchanged.
Malformed payload matrix (missing arrays, object instead of array, incomplete identity) remains covered in the governed-artifact suite.
correction2_toolOutputThroughTheRealProd.methodOutput: Unchanged and still honestly format-only. Its content_hash is a genuine sha256 from MethodOutputService, but this work does NOT recompute it: doing so would mean reimplementing that service's assembly of findings, sorting and rounding — a second definition of the same truth. No content-recompute claim is made.

correction3_noVacuousPass.whatWasWrong: `if (!harness) { expect(true).toBe(true); return; }` in the exe08 golden flow. A required real-database release gate reported 18/18 whether it exercised the ledger or found no database at all.
correction3_noVacuousPass.now: Throws EVIDENCE_MISSING with the reason and the remedy.

correction4_teardownThatHadStartedDyingS.finding: Sealing the ledger broke the exe08 harness cleanup: its first statement (DELETE FROM initiative_closure_evidence) threw, a blanket catch swallowed it, and every later statement was skipped. A green run left 12 organizations, 18 users and 78 initiatives behind and said nothing.
correction4_teardownThatHadStartedDyingS.fix: The ledger is cleared with TRUNCATE — DDL, requiring table ownership — in its own try block that logs on failure, so the rest of the teardown is no longer hidden behind one catch.
correction4_teardownThatHadStartedDyingS.foundBy: Counting rows in the database after a fully green regression run, not by a failing test.

rollback.product: git revert 95c864bc19 removes the reader, the four migrations and the suites, and restores canonical's service, route and two test files. Canonical had no closure-evidence chain, so there is nothing partial left behind.
rollback.database: All four migrations are additive: columns, constraints, two triggers, two functions. Dropping the triggers and constraints and the two added columns returns the table to its 934 shape without rewriting a row. The backfill is not reversed and does not need to be — snapshot_exempt only ever describes rows that predate the rule.
rollback.noDataLoss: Nothing in this change deletes or rewrites evidence content.

openItems.statement: method_output content is not independently verified, only its format. Recomputing it would duplicate MethodOutputService's assembly logic. Stated in the code; unchanged by this port.

Privileged retention is unimplemented on purpose. There is now NO way to remove an evidence row without table ownership. If a legal-retention or erasure obligation arises, it needs a dedicated database role and an operator workflow — a decision, not a code change to be made quietly.

The exe08 golden flow uses alg:none only inside the explicitly enabled test lifecycle harness. It proves lifecycle semantics, not production authentication; the closure-evidence suites separately use real HS256 tokens.
The corrected disposable-database teardown now leaves exact residue 0 while preserving production append-only semantics.
Fan-in requalification completed on exact reconciliation SHA 8883e410b8fa5ad4c67421f16804062cf40e8416.

environment.incidentsDuringTheRun: The Postgres container's checkpointer was SIGKILLed twice under write load (Docker VM memory, not disk — 21% used).
